judged_text: Google CalendarService updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback is dead code: the find fallback only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy and then searches for a calendar whose externalId equals undefined/null, which can never match, so calendar.events.update/delete is called with calendarId undefined and guaranteed fails; this path is reachable via legacy bookings and new bookings created in the no-credentialId branch of createAllCalendarEvents (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts ~256 and ~315)

adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent and deleteEvent, the fallback selection logic is incorrect: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` (and аналогous `calendarId` in delete) runs the `find` only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but then compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined/null`, so it will almost always return `undefined` and no longer falls back to the event’s destination calendar. This path is reachable because callers pass null/undefined externalCalendarId (e.g., EventManager.updateAndMergeCalendarEvents sets `calenderExternalId` to `null` when missing, and handleCancelBooking/delete uses reference.externalCalendarId which can be null). Result: updates/deletes may target an undefined calendarId or the wrong default calendar instead of the intended destination calendar.
